scope.implementation: The existing video-generation-engineering Skill, canonical planning core, quality/runtime/media/evidence helpers, tests, documentation, fixtures, local runtime evidence and portable distribution.
out_of_scope: Paid cloud generation, private-data upload, publication or external transfer without explicit authorization
Downloading major model weights or presenting unavailable capability as available
Semantic, physics, dialogue, lip-sync or long-form claims without current artifact observation

criteria.name: Baseline and preservation
criteria.acceptance: Audit current code, tests, runtime, artifacts and docs before changes; preserve mature behavior and failed evidence.

criteria.name: Canonical production chain
criteria.acceptance: Intent, canonical scene, shot graph, state, adaptation, prompt, execution, artifact, observation, transition QA, repair and assembly remain distinct linked boundaries.

criteria.name: LF-001 physical interaction
criteria.acceptance: A 10–15 second vehicle-entry fixture has causal phases, 13 independent acceptance dimensions, adjacent transition contracts and honest runtime/artifact status.

criteria.name: LF-002 dialogue closure
criteria.acceptance: A 20–30 second two-adult dialogue fixture separates semantics, voice, performance, lip-sync and mix, with speaker/listener and reaction-causality checks plus a known-bad listener-mouthing case.

criteria.name: LF-003 long-form closure
criteria.acceptance: A 45–60 second multi-shot fixture includes Scene Bible, continuity ledger, recurring characters, wardrobe, dialogue, object/high-risk interaction, audio, assembly, repair and checkpoint fields.

criteria.name: LF-004 honesty
criteria.acceptance: The optional 90–120 second ladder case exposes branches, recovery, provenance and editorial status without pretending it ran.

criteria.name: Anchors and reference decay
criteria.acceptance: Canonical source anchors outrank generated frames; drift signals select CONTINUE, RE_ANCHOR, RESET, SPLIT or REGENERATE with a smallest owner.

criteria.name: FLF capability
criteria.acceptance: First-only, last-only, combined endpoint, identity, object, motion and delivery checks are modeled with CONFIRMED/PARTIAL/UNSUPPORTED/UNKNOWN statuses.

criteria.name: Feature-scoped model profiles
criteria.acceptance: Capabilities bind to runtime version, node inventory, workflow, model, device, resources, evidence, date and limits; relevant changes invalidate only affected scope.

criteria.name: Adapter differential
criteria.acceptance: The same canonical plan compiles through Adapter A and Adapter B; intent, entities, locks, causal order, shot/state semantics and acceptance stay invariant while syntax/runtime may differ.

criteria.name: Prompt compiler
criteria.acceptance: Canonical prompt views preserve required semantic sections, expose omissions and mappings, use risk-shaped density, reject contradictions and select scoped negative constraints.

criteria.name: Interaction, ownership and vehicle state
criteria.acceptance: Contact phases, owner-before/contact/shared-contact/release/owner-after, vehicle state and observable physics are explicit; prose never substitutes for artifact QA.

criteria.name: Audio causality
criteria.acceptance: Dialogue, foley, ambience, room tone, vehicle/animal, music, transition and non-diegetic layers have timed source/cause/mix records with explicit intentional absence.

criteria.name: Mechanical media QA
criteria.acceptance: Readable file, duration, FPS, resolution, frame count, codec, audio stream/duration, decode, black, freeze, A/V alignment and hash are checked separately from semantics.

criteria.name: Semantic observation and continuity
criteria.acceptance: Explicit oracle/evidence/status/confidence/limitations observations cover semantic categories and the 14 continuity dimensions against exact artifact bytes.

criteria.name: Targeted repair
criteria.acceptance: Detect → localize → owner → minimal repair → regenerate → reobserve → reassemble is bounded by attempts, runtime, cost and human checkpoints; immutable history and downstream revalidation are preserved.

criteria.name: ComfyUI preflight and resources
criteria.acceptance: Version, nodes, schemas, model files, workflow inputs, extensions, VRAM/RAM/device and fallback statuses are observed before authorized submission.

criteria.name: Assembly and editorial gates
criteria.acceptance: Assembly validates accepted segment artifacts, format/duration/audio invariants and keeps technical, semantic and editorial acceptance separate.

criteria.name: Maturity and verdict
criteria.acceptance: Levels 0–5 and the allowed verdicts distinguish structural, runtime, audiovisual, bounded-production and repeatable evidence; scores cannot launder a required failure.

criteria.name: Architecture and progressive disclosure
criteria.acceptance: Core contracts own canonical state; scripts own deterministic validation; agents own directing/judgment; SKILL.md stays concise and routes only relevant references.

criteria.name: Evaluation library
criteria.acceptance: Metamorphic, property and known-bad fixtures cover the listed graph, timing, ownership, speaker, reference, artifact, workflow, repair, long-form and A/V failures.

criteria.name: Fresh independent review
criteria.acceptance: A new reviewer inspects the final candidate after implementation; pre/post fingerprints cover Skill, references, scripts, profiles, tests and distribution; any material mutation invalidates the review.

criteria.name: Portable distribution
criteria.acceptance: Fresh ZIP integrity, secrets/path/weights/media/link checks, external-CWD script execution, scoped profiles and template portability are recorded with SHA-256.

criteria.name: Documentation and traceability
criteria.acceptance: Canonical docs, ADRs, capability matrix, ladder, scorecard, report and control plane trace user goal → requirement → contract → implementation → test → runtime → artifact → observation → claim.

criteria.name: Exact final accounting
criteria.acceptance: The final report includes exact test count/failures/errors/skips/groups, required headings, independent 0–100 scores and explicit claims/non-claims.

criteria.name: Phase order and safety
criteria.acceptance: Phases A–M are executed or honestly blocked; safe local runtime is used where possible and paid APIs, uploads, weights and publication remain unauthorized.
